description: A dean of undergraduate studies must finalize an academic recovery contract for a college student on academic probation, including the student's course plan, enrollment conditions, support commitments, and approval documentation, with input from an academic advisor, registrar, student counselor, and financial-aid specialist.

shared_context.S1: A student who is below the college's academic-standing standard must receive a written academic recovery contract for the spring term.
shared_context.S2: The contract must state the student's enrollment plan, any conditions for continued enrollment, and the support services that will be monitored.
shared_context.S3: Dr. Morgan has authority to approve and sign the final academic recovery contract.
shared_context.S4: The student has asked to return to regular enrollment after the spring term and has submitted a draft plan for review.
shared_context.S5: As part of the college's routine pre-signoff review, Dr. Morgan asks the academic advisor, registrar, counselor, and financial-aid specialist for any information needed to finalize the contract.

PF1.text: Ms. Patel's degree audit shows that the student's only approved way to repair the failed major requirement this term is to repeat CHEM 201, a 4-credit course; the draft plan lists a different elective, and she identified the mismatch during her advising review but has not yet revised the draft.

PF2.text: Mr. Brooks confirmed that the student's academic-standing reinstatement requires 12 completed credits during the spring term, not merely enrollment in an unspecified full-time load; he verified this in the registrar's standing rule but has not entered the condition in the contract template.

PF3.text: Ms. Nguyen confirmed with the student that a documented caregiving obligation makes 12 credits manageable only when at least 6 credits are delivered asynchronously; she recorded this in her counseling file but has not sent the delivery condition to the dean.

PF4.text: Mr. Ellis confirmed that the student's financial-aid appeal remains eligible only if the recovery contract requires advisor meetings every two weeks for the first 8 weeks of the term; he received that condition from the aid committee but has not attached it to the academic contract.

acceptance_conditions: The recovery contract must be approved.
CHEM 201 must count for exactly 4 credits.
The student must complete exactly 12 spring credits.
At least 6 of the spring credits must be asynchronous.
The contract must require advisor meetings every two weeks for the first 8 weeks.
The signed contract must be formally filed.

content_checks.C6: any(c['type'] == 'biweekly_advising' and c['detail'] == 'every two weeks for 8 weeks' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The degree-audit finding changes the required course from the draft elective to CHEM 201 and changes the required course value to exactly 4 credits.
The registrar's standing rule changes the enrollment condition from an unspecified full-time load to exactly 12 completed spring credits.
The counseling record changes the delivery plan by requiring at least 6 of the 12 credits to be asynchronous.
The aid-committee condition changes the support commitment to advisor meetings every two weeks for the first 8 weeks.
